title: 夏日绝句
author: 李清照
intro: Twenty characters with a sharp edge. Li Qingzhao praises the defeated hero Xiang Yu, who chose death rather than flee across the river — a pointed rebuke to a Song court that kept running south from the invaders.
analysis: 这首诗一般认为写于宋朝南渡之后。金兵攻占北方，宋朝皇帝和大臣一路往南逃，不敢收复失地。李清照借古讽今：活着就要做人中的豪杰，死了也要做鬼中的英雄。接着她想到项羽——秦末的英雄，兵败退到乌江边，有人劝他渡江回江东重新开始，他觉得没脸见江东父老，不肯过江，在江边自尽。“至今思项羽”表面上是怀念古人，其实是在问：今天的人为什么只会逃跑？诗只有二十个字，没有一个字直接批评朝廷，但对比非常鲜明。一位女诗人写出这样刚烈的句子，所以特别有名，前两句今天还常被引用。
analysisEn: This short poem is usually dated to the years after the Song court fled south. The Jurchen Jin had taken northern China, and the emperor and his ministers kept retreating rather than fight to win it back. Li Qingzhao answers with history. The first couplet is a statement of values: in life, be a hero among men; in death, be a hero among ghosts. Then she turns to Xiang Yu, the great warlord who lost to the founder of the Han dynasty around 202 BC. Trapped at the Wu River, he was offered a boat to escape east of the Yangtze, where he could raise a new army. He refused — he could not face the families of the soldiers he had lost — and died on the riverbank. “To this day I think of Xiang Yu, who would not cross to the east” looks like simple admiration for an ancient hero. But the contrast is obvious to any reader: Xiang Yu would not run, and the Song court did nothing but run. The poem never criticises anyone by name, which makes the point sharper. Strong, bare lines like these, from a poet best known for delicate love lyrics, are why the first two lines are still quoted today.
background: Li Qingzhao (1084–c. 1155) fled south after the Jin conquest of the north in 1127. The poem is traditionally linked to 1129, around the time her husband abandoned his post in Jiankang (Nanjing) during a mutiny — some read it as aimed at him as well as at the court.
pronunciation: 生当作 dāng（应当）；死亦为 wéi（做、成为）；项羽 Xiàng Yǔ。
version: 采用通行文本，题一作《乌江》。异文：“作”“为”二字一本互换（“生当为人杰，死亦作鬼雄”）。

lines.lit: In life, one should be a hero among men;
lines.en: Alive, be the bravest of the living;

lines.lit: in death, also be a hero among ghosts.
lines.en: dead, be the boldest of the dead.

lines.lit: To this day, I think of Xiang Yu,
lines.en: I still think of Xiang Yu

lines.lit: who was unwilling to cross to the east of the river.
lines.en: who would not cross the river to save himself.

words.en: an outstanding person; a hero among men

words.note: 雄：英雄。现代汉语“英雄”“雄壮”。

words.en: Xiang Yu (232–202 BC), warlord who lost to the founder of the Han
words.note: 成语“破釜沉舟”“四面楚歌”“霸王别姬”都和他有关。
现代汉语仍用，如“不肯”“肯定”。

words.en: east of the Yangtze — Xiang Yu’s home region
words.note: 成语“无颜见江东父老”就出自项羽的故事。

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 乌江是生死的分界：过江可以逃命，不过江就是死。项羽选择了不过。
imagery.en: The river is the line between life and death: crossing meant escape, and Xiang Yu refused to cross.
